THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, PRAYING TO  MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 06.10.2012, PASSED IN  MVC NO.408/2011, ON THE FILE OF THE DISTRICT JUDGE AND  MEMBER, MACT, GADAG, BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AND  TO EXONERATE THE LIABILITY OF THE OWNER OF VEHICLE BY  FIXING THE LIABILITY ON THE INSURANCE COMPANY TO PAY  COMPENSATION, BY ALLOWING THIS APPEAL, ETC.,.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397  MFA No. 20803 of 2013  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 06.10.2012, passed by the District and Sessions Judge and Member, MACT, Gadag, in MVC No.408/2011, seeking enhancement of compensation as well as questioning the liability fixed on the owner of the truck.
2. The factum of accident and injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident are not in dispute in this case.

entities.text: District and Sessions Judge and Member, MACT, Gadag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
4.

The tribunal while awarding compensation has fixed liability on the owner of the truck on the reason that the driver of the truck was holding driving licence to drive the light motor vehicle but the truck is a heavy motor vehicle.
From the evidence on record it is proved that the driver was holding licence to drive light motor vehicle only NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397 and the truck is a heavy transport vehicle.
Therefore the tribunal is correct in holding that the owner is liable to pay compensation by exonerating the insurance company.

5. However even though as per sub-section (2) of section 149 of the M.V.Act, the insurance company is able to establish his defence but as per sub-section (1), (5) and (7) of section 149 of the M.V.Act,
and also as per the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of PAPPU AND OTHERS vs. VINOD KUMAR LAMBA AND ANOTHER reported in (2018) 3 SCC 208;
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED vs. SWARAN SINGH AND OTHERS reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297; and also as per the Full Bench decision of this Court in the case of NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED vs. YELLAVVA AND ANOTHER reported in 2020 ACJ 2560,
the insurance company shall satisfy the claim at the first instance to the claimants and then recover it from the owner of the tractor.

sentences.text: Therefore pay and recovery order is made.
6. In the present case the claimant has suffered the following injuries.
7. The doctor has assessed the percentage of disability at 30% towards left lower limb and the tribunal considered 15% towards whole body.
The claimant is a labour by profession.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, it is just and proper to take 22% as functional disability towards whole body.
The claimant was aged 40 years old at the time of accident.

Accordingly as per the NC:
2023:KHC-D:12397 age group mentioned in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, and as per the Division Bench judgment of this Court in New India Assurance Company Vs. Abdul S/o Mehaboob Tahasildar in MFA No.103807/2016 C/w. MFA Nos.103835/2016 & 103807/2018 and as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2023) 3 SCC 439, even in the case of injuries, certain income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

sentences.text: Since the claimant has suffered significant disability, due to fracture injuries stated above, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
8. The accident is caused on 16.12.2011 and therefore, in the absence of proof of income, notional income would be Rs.6,000/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

Considering NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397 the age of the claimant as on the date of accident,
the appropriate applicable multiplier is 15.
Therefore, the loss of future earning capacity due to disability is re-assessed and quantified as Rs.3,32,640/- (Rs.6,000 + 40% x 22% x 12 x 15).

9. Further, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, a compensation of Rs.85,000/-
towards injuries pain and suffering, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities are awarded.
The compensation of Rs.38,230/- awarded by the tribunal towards medical expenses and hospital charges is as per the actual bills and receipts produced; therefore, the same is kept intact.

Further,
Rs.15,000/- towards incidental expenses like food, nourishment, travelling, attendant charges, etc.,
and Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during laid up and treatment period for a period of five months, is awarded.

10. Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397 Sl. Heads.

Amount in No. (Rs.)
1. Towards injuries, pain and 85,000 suffering.

3 . Towards loss of amenities.
Towards loss of income during 30,000 laid up period and medical treatment period.

5. Towards incidental charges like 15,000 attendant charges, food, nourishment,
conveyance, etc.,.
6. Towards loss of future earning 3,32,640 capacity.
Total: 5,40,870 11.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,40,870/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.2,82,130/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Since insurance company is exonerated from liability to pay compensation, in order to protect interest of the claimant, it is directed that the insurance company shall satisfy the claim to the claimant at the first instance NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397 within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and then recover it from the owner of the truck.

Liberty is given to the insurance company to file execution petition directly before the concerned executing Court and may seek for attachment of moveable and immoveable properties or both till the recovery of amount.

13. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 06.10.2012, passed by the District and Sessions Judge and Member, MACT, Gadag, in MVC No.408/2011 stands modified.
iii) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,40,870/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.2,82,130/- awarded by the Tribunal.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12397 iv) The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 37 days in filing the appeal.
